text_data.shortbiography: Italian physician, also known as Jérôme Cardan, famed from 1526; by age 50 he ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
LMR quotes "Giralmo Cardano: Book of My Life," translated from the Latin by Jean Stoner, 1930, p.4, "I was born normally September 24, 1501 when the first hour of the night was more than half run but less than two-thirds." (September 25, Florentine time, 6:40 PM LAT) All editions of the "De Colsolations Liber III, Vol 1" give 1500, but in his own horoscope he gives the date and hour as above.

Biography: Anthony Grafton, "Cardano's Cosmos: The Worlds and Works of a Renaissance Astrologer," Harvard University Press, 1999.

A review of this book by Shelley Jordan can be seen at:
http://cura.free.fr/books.html

text_data.shortbiography: Spanish cellist and conductor, known for his innovative technique, masterful ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Charles Harvey quotes him in AQ, Spring/1968. Philip Lucas quotes B.R. for December 30, 1876, 8:00 PM. Casals himself said that the December 30 date is wrong, that it was the 29th. (For some unknown reason Pablo's father was two days late reporting Pablo's birth to the Roman Catholic Church, and so the official registered date of his birth is December 31.)
Update 14-jun-2012: The biography ''Pablo Casals'' by Robert Baldock, Page 21, says: "The infant born to Dona Pilar Defillo i Amiguet and her husband Carlos Casals in the late afternoon of Friday, 29 December 1876 emerged with its umbilical cord twisted around its neck, its face turning blue from the constriction."
What is meant by 'late afternoon' in the context of Spain is not clear.

text_data.shortbiography: American singer who was a world famed crooner for his mellow baritone. His ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Judy Wisniewski quotes author Gary Giddins, "Bing Crosby: A Pocketful of Dreams, The Early Years (1903-1940)." On p.30 he states that Bing’s mother Kate delivered Bing, her fourth son on Sunday, May 3, 1903. On p. 31 he mentions that Bing's younger sister, Mary Rose, was born on May 3, 1906. Mary Rose insisted on having the day to herself. Peace prevailed when Harry's (Bing’s) birthday was advanced by twenty-four hours. In later years Mary Rose would produce the family bible in which their father had assigned May 2nd to Harry. 
The dilemma continues on p.30. Kate, who had just turned thirty, and Harry Sr., finally established in the city's middle class, decided that this boy's arrival merited a public announcement. For the first time, they alerted the newspapers of a newborn. When the Daily Ledger failed to print the item in "City news in brief" until May 5, implying with the word ‘yesterday’ that the great event had taken place on May 4, Kate stipulated the correct date for its rival, the Tacoma Daily News. "Mr. and Mrs. H. L. Crosby are receiving congratulations on the arrival of a son at their household May 3 (third) and requested a correction from the ledger, which appeared on May 7." For all the decisiveness with which May 3, 1903, was flagged as Harry Lillis Crosby's birthdate, the date proved controversial in and out of family circles. In all official accounts (generated by Paramount, Decca, the Crosby offices, and most insistently, Bing himself) it was altered by one day and one year to May 2nd, 1904!
Steinbrecher quoted Crosby's British fan club for 5/03/1903, "from baptism" (???)
(Formerly, the data was reported from the biography by Bob Thomas, "Bing," 1977, which read, "Some said 1901, the studio said 1904, Bing just shrugged and went along with it. After his death a parish priest said that his birth records gave May 2, 1903." Various sources gave May 1, May 2, May 3, May 4, 1901, 1902, 1903, 1904.) 
The time of 4:00 PM is from Sabian Symbols No.232 (which had 1904).
Starkman rectified to 3 May 1903 16.24.56 PST

text_data.shortbiography: Greek opera singer, noted for her glorious voice, stirring acting ability, and ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
B.C. in hand from William Henry, July 1995, with 2 Dec 1923, no birth time. Same information quoted by Ann Parker from the biography by Nadia Stanciott "Maria Callas Remembered," E.P. Dutton, 1987, p.44, "Sophie Cecelia Kalos, apparently shortened by a member of the staff of Manhattan's 5th Ave hospital from her full name, Kalogeropoulos. Even the mother's maiden name, Evangelia Demetroadis had been shorted to Demos and her more familiar first name, Litza." The time 7:07 am comes as calculated time from her mom's quote of "dawn." 
Over the years, various quotes have been given as "from her" or "from the family," for times ranging before and after daybreak. Luis Ortet writes, October 2000, "According to French astrologer Andre Barbault, when Callas ordered her horoscope at "Astroflash" in Paris, she wrote that she was born at 6 AM, given in "Astralites des Femmes Ilustres," Editions du Rocher, 1998, pp 316.
Note 24 April 2012 by atr:
Manfred Gregor, Hamburg, reports that he has seen a document in Paris, shown to him by Michel Gauquelin, where Callas herself states her birth date as 3 December, 6:00 am. French collector Didier Geslain has the same date and time, quoting as source 'herself'. Because Callas lived in Paris and had personal contact with local astrologers, we follow the French connection Barbault/Gauquelin/Geslain. Many published biographies give 2 Dec, also Wikipedia. Wikipedia notes "(biographer) Slonimsky and others have argued that, despite her birth certificate, she was actually born on 3 December". 
In the book 'My daughter' her mother, Evangelia Callas, writes: "My daughter Maria began life in a storm ... The day she was born, the fourth of December 1923, there was a snow storm such as I have never seen before." This is quoted by Michael Scott in his book 'Maria Meneghini Callas'. Scott writes that the birth certificate (also on file at Astrodienst) gives 2nd December, and that New York meteorological reports show for the 2nd cold but dry weather, no snow, no precipitation at all. Scott further quotes Callas' 1957 autobiography, that she, while her passport stated 2nd, preferred the fourth, partly because it was St Barbara's day, but also because her mother told her so and 'I have to believe what my mother says.'

text_data.shortbiography: American politician and diplomat who served as the 67th United States secretary ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
'''Most recent entry at the bottom.'''
[wiki-code]
Nov 2000: Celeste Longacre quotes her for 8 PM.

Kt Boehrer writes (ACT online 11/2000), "I can confirm the 8:00 PM data. I have used this data for years (since before Bill became the presidential candidate the first time) and I received it from a very dear friend and good client who knew them well whose identity I cannot reveal."

However Eileen Applegate quotes an article from the Chicago Sun Times stating, "Her mother went into Edgewater hospital after midnight and Hillary was born early on the morning of October 26th."

In an article in "Horoscope" magazine, November 1998, by Frances C. McEvoy: "Mother states in article to 'Chicago Sun Times' in 1992 that Hillary was "born in time for breakfast."

Basil Fearrington relates in January 2001, "A musician friend of mine played in the Democratic fund raiser for Al Gore in Manhattan this past summer. Afterwards he got a chance to talk to Hillary. Knowing my on-going love affair with astrological data (he is a student of mine), he asked Hillary what time she was born. Her exact words were, " I know it was very close to 8 AM, 4-5 minutes before or after."

Alice Mason called on 16 January 2003 to report that she had talked to the Clinton Democratic Office in NY and was told by a helpful associate (who wished to remain nameless) that Hillary Clinton was born at a recorded 8:02 AM.

Biography: Laura Ingraham, "The Hillary Trap: Looking for Power in All the Wrong Places," 2000, has the time 8:00pm "according to herself."

In August 2005, a source who wishes to remain anonymous wrote: "I had asked Hillary Clinton whether she was born at 8 PM; she replied " I think so". Earlier I had asked her, her time of birth and she kept mum.

Dana Haynes reports that one website lists "Born at the stroke of midnight (12 AM CST) but no source was given.

The AstroDatabank website comments on her chart include an unverified claim from Zayin Cohen claiming to be quoting from birth certificate saying "I can say that I have the correct Birth Time. 26 OCT 1947 2:18 AM Chicago,IL."

In early Feb 2008 Arlan Wise wrote to the ISAR e-zine vol. 477 the following: "HILLARY CLINTON >from Arlan Wise to Marguerite dar Boggia.:I know this is hearsay, but, my chiropractor has treated Bill and Hillary when they come here (Martha's Vineyard) in the summer. She told me she had a conversation with Hillary about how they have the same astrology-both Scorpios with Pisces moons and both Leo rising. I haven't seen a time that gives Hillary a Leo ascendant but that's what she says she has. It definitely negates the 8:02 am time and adds to the confusion."

26 Sep 2016: A posting by Mark on the Skyscript forum states: "However, I corresponded with Zayin Cohen a few weeks ago. Zayin Cohen then claimed the time he had actually found was 02.08 am not 02.18am. He said it was incorrectly reported on ADB and elsewhere." On the day before, ISAR anncounced that at an upcoming conference on 16 Oct 2016, astrologer Marc Penfield will report his findings from the Illinois birth registry, regarding Hillary's time of birth. It is rumored that he will confirm Cohen's report.
Update 11 Nov 2018: In a text exchange with Patrick Wilson in August 2015, Zayin Cohen now claimed to have seen a birth certificate with the time 1:18. His claims carry the smell of 'fake news.'

On 29 Sep. 2016, Steven Stuckey writes by email: "Below is a copy of an article published in the Chicago Sun Times on Jan 17, 1993. I believe it is the long sought-after article that Francis McEvoy and others have referred to and apparently also mis-quoted. It was found on August 15, 2016 while I was researching this with the reference desk of the Chicago Public Library, that has the Sun Times on computer for many years in the past. The important and pertinent part is approximately 10 lines down where it states that Hillary's mother arrived at the hospital "early" and that Hillary was born 12 hours later. This obviously implies a PM birth and not AM, as has long been inferred by astrologers. I personally contacted Lynn Sweet, who wrote the 1993 article and she is still working for the Sun Times and now their chief correspondent in Washington DC. I spoke with her twice on the phone and questioned her about her sources on the article. Unfortunately, too much time has passed and she can no longer remember how she determined that Dorothy Rodham arrived "early", or even what exactly "early" means. Ms. Sweet did not interview Hillary or her mother for the article but she does (vaguely) remember reading the 12 hour labour info from some sort of document, which she remembered as the birth document. But again, she can provide no notes of how she came up with this data and we are not likely to get any more info on this in the future (although she said that she would call me if she could remember anything else)." [end of Stuckey email] A scan of the Chicago Sun Times article can be seen [https://kannonmcafee.files.wordpress.com/2016/10/hrc-sun-times-jan93-article-p1.jpg here].

2 Oct 2016: In an interview on [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-ffCemlJ7V0 Youtube], Marc Penfield claims that in a phone interview with an employee of the birth registry, the time 2:18 am was confirmed by the registrar. Rating remains DD until copy of BC is presented.

Update 14 Oct 2016: according to an article in the [https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/local/wp/2016/10/14/this-is-not-to-be-trusted-astrologers-are-battling-over-hillary-clintons-true-birth-time/ Washington Post] penfield has withdrawn his claim to have confirmed the 2:18 am time via a phone call with the Chucago reg

2 March 2023: Birth certificate in hand from Viktor E. The hour digit of the handwritten time is not too clearly read. It could look like a 6, but may possibly be a sloppily written 10. See the B.C. on the right. 
16 March 2023: Alois Treindl: The reading of the birth hour as 6 or 10 is not 100% clear. There are three other digits 6 on the document, which all have a rounded back. The vertical stroke in the birth hour is very straight. There is one other number 10 in the document. If it had a thick base line like the birth time, it might look just the same. After careful deliberation with some data researchers, we hold the reading as 6 for the most likely.
I have removed earlier rectifications from the source notes, as a birth certificate makes these no longer meaningful.

text_data.shortbiography: American politician who served as the 42nd president of the United States from ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Note in hand from Mrs. Virginia Kelley, Clinton's mom, to Shelley Ackerman with the time hand-written. She gave the same data in an interview with "Family Circle" magazine of 2/02/1993, p.23.
(Virginia Miller quoted Clinton for the time of 7:30 AM given without hesitation.
(David Maraniss "First in his Class" stateed that Clinton was born one hour after dawn, "Details of his birth from Edith Cassidy's records, in possession of her niece, Myra Irvin. As his grandmother was a nurse who worked at the local hospital, she would probably have taken her daughter into the hospital for the birth." (Source detailed in the Notes section of the biography.) (Dawn is 5:24 AM)
(Kathy Forrest called 10/13/96 to relate that she had talked to Clinton's mom about four years back and that she had said he was born at 7:30 AM. Kathy asked "Are you sure?" and the mom said "I should be, I'm his mother." Virginia Kelley relates in the Maraniss biography that her Bill was an eight-month baby, despite his birth weight of nearly 8 1/2 lbs. Her husband, Blythe, returned from Italy where he was stationed eight months before Bill was born.
(Edith Custer sent a long letter from Rowena Wall dated 6/121/95 in which she related that when Clinton began his campaign she asked her mom, who lives in Pine Bluff, AR, to see if she could get his birth data. Her mom replied that she found the data in a book in the library that had the birth certificate in it, giving 3:44 AM. When this information was printed in AFA DX No.104 (5/02/92), both Mark Lerner and Ken Irving called the library but were told that no such book was there. When Rowena Wall asked her mom to double-check, the alleged biography could not be found, making the quote impossible to verify.)

text_data.shortbiography: Polish classical composer and virtuoso pianist of the Romantic era, he was ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
March 1, 1810: David Fisher quotes Valerie Matthews letter from Dariusz Proskurnicki in Poland, "Chopin himself presented his date as the 1st of March, 1810, as presented in his letter dated 1/16/1833 to the Head of the Literary Society in Paris. The same date is given in the letters of his Scottish pupil Jane W. Stirling, saying that "his parents made an error of eight days when they went to the registry office some weeks after his birth." 
Juan Revilla quotes Bernard Gavoty, "Frederic Chopin, Charles Scribner’s Sons, NY 1977 for March 1. "This date was given by Chopin himself as told him by his father and this is the date that was celebrated by his family. In a letter to the Societe Litteraire Polonaise of Paris, in a letter dated January 11, 1833, Chopin says he was born March 1, 1810." 

January 22, 1810: Modern Astrology 5/1909 gave Jan 22 "from his father's record," same from M. Karosowski "Chopin, Life and Letters," 1906. Library reference points out the discrepancy of many years standing, that of a date of January 22 or February 22, 1810. 

February 22, 1810: His B.C. and Baptism were found many years after his death, both written in April 1810, both giving February 22, 1810. All accounts quote his father's record for 6:00 PM. Guy de Pourtalis "Chopin, Le Poete" gives Feb 22, same in Wemyss and in Sabian Symbols No.201. Biography: Henri Bidou, "Chopin" gave Feb 22, 1810, 6:00 PM, Warsaw. The baptismal certificate, dated April 23 1810 says he was born February 22, 1810 and the birth certificate, in Polish, written by the parish priest Jan Duchnowsky, says explicitly Feb 22, 1810, and adds the exact hour: 6 p.m.

Further confusion was caused by different evidence, such as the inscription on the urn where his heart is conserved in Warsaw, which reads March 2, 1809. Chopin’s first biographer, Maurizy Karasowski, proposed March 1 1809. The "Biographie universelle des musiciens" by Francoise Fetis, published in Paris in 1835, gives February 8, 1810.
Starkman rectified to 1 March 1810 17.13.40 LMT Asc 7Vir09'

text_data.sourcenotes:
LMR quotes biographer Doris Agee, "Edgar Cayce on ESP" (p.55) "As in this body, born 3/18/1877, three minutes past three o'clock." Hugh Lynn Casey "Venture Inward," same data, 3:03 PM. Given as CST, equivalent of 3:20 PM LMT.
Thomas Sugrue "There is a River" quotes his grandmom (p.59) "I heard the first squall you made at three o'clock exactly." 
(R.H. Oliver quotes his son for 3:30 PM. Sugrue used 3:20 PM in an article in Astrology Review 3/47. Zip Dobyns quotes 1:30 PM given as family records from a librarian at the Cayce Foundation.)
Michael Rideout adds, 7/2001, "Report 4 for Reading 254-2 quotes a letter which Edgar Cayce wrote to Ms. 516. A date of September 16, 1935 is given, but I'm not sure if that was the date of Edgar Cayce's letter, or the date when Report 4 was added to the file:
> "...I was born on March 18, 1877, in Hopkinsville, Christian County, Kentucky, at 1:30 o'clock on a Sunday afternoon. However, I have had several astrologers tell me it was impossible for me to have been born at that time, else I would have been a girl. But this is the actual record from my parents, the physician, and the birth certificate record..."
Thus, according to Edgar Cayce's own account, his birth certificate listed his time of birth as 1:30 p.m. The kind of time isn't mentioned, but LMT was observed before November 18, 1883.
Report 9 for Reading 2441-3 is Edgar's reply to Mrs.2441, which is dated December 31, 1941. In it, he has the following to say: Would be glad for your friend [Raymond McDermott] to give me a horoscope reading. The information, I believe - is Mar. 18th, 1877, 3.20 P.M., Long. 87-30, Lat. 36-45, Hopkinsville, Ky. Would like to see a copy if might, as you can imagine have seen quite a number of these and very few agree one with the other."
Michael Rideout, 2/2002, writes, "Cayce's location of birth is usually given as Hopkinsville, Kentucky, but 
information on the CD-ROM says he was born on a farm near Beverly, Kentucky, about seven miles south of Hopkinsville. I'm therefore using 87W30, 36N45 
for the coordinates."
Starkman rectified to 14.15.16 LMT
Note 30 May 2015: 3:03 cst or 3:20 lmt mentioned several times above, but 3:03 lmt was actually entered. This has been corrected now.

text_data.shortbiography: English comic actor, filmmaker, and composer who rose to fame in the era of ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
LMR quotes Chaplin in ''My Autobiography'' (1964), page 14: "I was born on 16 April 1889, at eight O'clock at night, in East Lane, Walworth. Soon after, we moved to West Square, St George's Road, Lambeth. According to Mother my world was a happy one."

Sy Scholfield notes that 15 April is given in birth notices. For example, ''The Era'' (London), 11 May 1889, page 18, gives this date, born to "the wife of Charles Chaplin, nee Lily Harley" (see at left). The biography, ''Chaplin, His Life and Art'' by David Robinson (McGraw-Hill, 1985), page xxiv, quotes Chaplin's birth notice in ''The Magnet'', 11 May 1889, for "the 15th ultimo," i.e. 15 April. There is no entry for Chaplin in the England and Wales Birth Index and no known birth certificate. 

Other references: born in Smethwick (Birmingham) or Chaplin could be named Thomstein and be born in Fontainebleau, France. Starkman rectified to 16 April 1889 19.40.48 GMT Asc 5Sco17'.

For date of birth he wrote 17. Rumely Co. on a business trip through Europe and northern Africa . Maree accompanied him on this tour . Divorced in June , 1916. Second marriage , June 30 , 1917 , to Captain Clyde Galen Chaney , formerly City Editor of the La- Porte Argus , now commanding Co. B , 151st Infantry." (''Genealogy of the Martin family'' by Charles William Francis and Alice Brewer Shedd, Dalcassian Publishing Company, 1918, page 194).

Bob Skeetz quotes Carroll Righter for a Scorpio ASC, probably a solar chart. Steinbrecher quotes Cronkite's secretary for the same date, no record of time. Just after Cronkite's death in July 2009, PT changed the birth date from 14 November 1916 to 4 November 1916 to be consistent with information in his book "A Reporter's Life" and his obituary in the NY Times. The 14 November date was probably a typo and should have been 04 November.
Starkman rectified to 03.30.24 CST Asc 0Lib50'.
Sy Scholfield provided birth notice, ''The Leavenworth Post'' (Leavenworth, Kansas), 4 November 1916, page 5, "Dr. and Mrs. Walter Leland Cronkite of St. Joseph, Mo., announce the birth of a son, this morning." Mrs. Cronkite was originally from Leavenworth, their son was born in St. Joseph.

text_data.sourcenotes:
Marion March quotes birth certificate. ''CAO Times'' states that the time (normally CST) was set to EST for business reasons. 
No confirmation could be found for this claim. Plain is in the western part of the state, in Sumter county's western part. The CST/EST boundary goes across Sumter county, and Plains was clearly in the CST section. It followed [https://www.appenmedia.com/opinion/opinion-when-georgia-had-two-time-zones/article_0bb3e6c4-9c84-11eb-a1f5-6b1a42a8e61a.html Central time] until 21 March 1941.

In June 2019 Sy Scholfield provided photo of birth record stating time of birth as "seven A.M." The record is held at the Jimmy Carter Presidential Library and Museum and a photo of it was published online by Sage Scott [https://everydaywanderer.com/jimmy-carter-museum]. The Rodden Rating was thus upgraded to "BC/BR in hand."

Different reports give his birth place as Cajamarca, Peru or Sao Paulo, Brazil.\n[wiki-code]In July 2014, Lepoivre mentions Kannon McAfee as a source for 9 am birthtime. On 12 July 2014 McAffee wrote on the forum:"I possess a photocopy of the original birth certificate from Cajamarca, Peru. For years times around 2 pm have been passed around after the 5 March 1973 TIME magazine cover article. It appears that a TIME magazine Peruvian correspondent glanced at the birth manifest record made the next day at 2:30 PM and mistook this for the birth time. In fact the document clearly shows that the date of birth was on 25 December 1925 at "nueve a.m." Nine AM. ". A day later he posted a copy of the BC on the forum.\n

text_data.shortbiography: Cuban liberator who successfully overthrew President Batista's government 1 ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
John McKay-Clements quotes a new biography "Castro" 3/96, "He swears it was August 13, 1926, 2:00 AM."
"Fidel and Religion" (Simon & Schuster, 1987) is the record of 23 hours of talks with Frei Betto. On p.2 it mentions in parenthisis that Castro was born August 13, 1926.
Tad Szulc "Fidel Castro, A Critical Portrait" (Hutchinson, London, 1987) "For years there has been disagreement of 1926 or 1927. He himself swears 1926. Even the Soviet press gave the wrong data in a lengthy biography published in 1963 and the error has been maintained in the Cuban news. The confusion stems from a change made in his school records when he lost three months of classes because of post-appendectomy complications. It was at Manacas that Castro was born (p.96), a large sugarcane-cattle estate located in the municipality of Biran in the northern Oriente province coast, about 25 miles south of the Bay of Nipe and the same east of Dos Rios. In any case, he was born about 2:00 AM on 13 August, 1926, weighing ten pounds."
Monica Hable Dimino writes in April 1993, "One of my students spoke to Castro during a dinner reception and asked his data. He said, "I was born the 13th of August of 1926 at 4:44 AM In Vertientes, Cuba, my mother told me." Dimino later corrected the birth location as Veranorientes, just outside of Santiago.
"Peter Bourne "Fidel" (1986, p.14) "He was born on his father's farm, Las Manacas, near the village of Biran not far from the town of Mayari in the Oriente Province. He weighted 12 pounds at birth. The third of three illigitimate kids, he was six when his parents married. He was too young to enrole in school so they pushed his age back a year to make him eligible, and the date of 1926 has been given ever since. He himself gives 1926 and the Cuban government gives 1926, but the year of his birth was 1927.
AQ Winter/1960 quotes Lavagnini "from official government sources" for 8/13/1926, 1:00 PM. 
Bruna Serrotti wrote in Mercury Hour 7/85 "I read that Castro was born 8/12/1926, Wrong! It was 7/26/26 in Havana, information from the Cuban Embassy in New York."
Boris Cristoff gives 1927, "When Alina Castro came to my house as a consultant she said his father was almost 29 years when she was born. She was born in on 19/3/56, 7h00 Habana, so Fidel was born in 1927. " In early September 2005, Tony Martinez writes via e-mail," I know the NBC News Bureau chief in Havana, Cuba. I asked her to research this and she told me the following - Fidel Castro Ruz, August 13, 1926, 2:00 AM Biran, Oriente Cuba. Time of birth comes directly from his autobiography - http://www.wordswithoutborders.org/article.php?lab=AutobiographyCastro: '...These whirlwinds can get to be five to eight kilometers high and three hundred kilometers across and last an average of eight days. But I couldn’t have known I was being pushed into this world on that night of August 13, 1926, around two in the morning, nor that there was a hurricane at a reasonable distance from Birán..'."

Sy Scholfield quotes from "The Origins of the Cuban Revolution Reconsidered" by Samuel Farber (University of North Carolina Press, 2006), p. 182: "While Fidel Castro's official birth date is August 13, 1926, he was actually born on August 13, 1927. His father had Fidel's original birth certificate changed so that he could enroll at the Belen high school (Claudia Furiati, Fidel Castro: La Historia Me Absolvera. trans. Rosa S. Corgatelli [Barcelona: Plaza Janes, 2003], 48-49, 81)." 
Scholfield notes that Castro's time of birth is stated in various news reports and biographies, eg.: "Havana, Aug 15 (EFE).- Commenting on his 73rd birthday Friday, Cuban President Fidel Castro said it was the "best" he had ever had ... 'I believe I was born at two in the morning,' Castro said. 'And that explains my guerrilla tendencies, since I was born at night.'" ("CASTRO: "I'VE NEVER HAD A BETTER BIRTHDAY," 15 August 1999, EFE News Service).
Starkman rectified to 13 August 1927 02.00.01.10 EST Asc 29Gem30'

B.R. in hand from Steinbrecher on which the year is clearly typed as 1929; however, Jim Gorham in 2004 writes to PT: I have 2 good sources which suggest the Dossier year of birth may be in error: 1) A University of California memorium for Donald Ray Cressey (1919 to 1987), Professer Emeritus, a sociologist who is credited with writing some of the books mentioned in the bio. PT speculates that the clerk in the birth records office mistyped year of birth as it is unusual for people to say they are born 10 years BEFORE their official birth time. 2) The California Death Index. Place of birth matches (Minnesota); month and day of birth match (April 27), but the year is again 1919.

In October 2017: year of birth changed to 1919, assuming 1929 was a mistype as the online biographies all seem to have 1919 as birth year. His Wikipedia bio also states that he got his Ph.D. from Indiana University in 1950. If born in 1929, he would have been 21. If in 1919, 31.

Her autobiography, "Second Act," 1996, gives "morning."
On 9 Feb 2018 Sy Scholfield changed rating from DD to A, quoting Collins in an online "Diary" entry published on ''The Spectator'' website, Feb 2018: "I’ve been meaning to write a ''Spectator'' diary since the summer but as a Gemini with Aries rising I find I have the annoying trait (just the one?) of being too easily distracted..." [https://www.spectator.co.uk/2018/02/joan-collins-want-to-know-why-all-the-oscar-films-are-boring-ill-tell-you/]. Scholfield notes that the England and Wales Birth Registration Index has Joan H. Collins registered in the district of Paddington in the July-Sep quarter of 1933.
On 11 Feb 2018 Scholfield downgraded the rating from A to C, having received an email from Frank C. Clifford: "Her astrologer is a friend of mine and apparently Collins doesn’t know her birth time (except for it being in the morning) but she seems to be happy with that combo [Gemini with Aries rising]."
Starkman rectified to 03.32.00 BST Asc 18Ari58'

text_data.sourcenotes:
In December 2023 Dave Campbell emailed the link to a Youtube video showing the birth certificate in the first few minutes [https://youtu.be/tS42AFQCRn4]. Greenpoint Hospital is recorded as the place of birth.

Previously, Criss was quoted in his autobiography, "Makeup to Breakup: My Life in Kiss" (2012), at the beginning of chapter one: "I entered the world on December 20, 1945, feet first, ass backward, a breech baby." No time given. Data downgraded from "A" to "DD", because the time quoted by Criss at an earlier date was given at the same time as the erroneous birth year.

Also previously, Steinbrecher quoted J. Swartzberg, from Criss over the radio for 13:30 (1:30 PM), 20 December 1947. The "Almanac of Famous People" incorrectly gives 1947 as do many other written references.

text_data.shortbiography: Spanish Princess, the daughter and second of three children of King Juan Carlos ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Michaël Mandl quotes Jany Bessière from birth record [http://www.mandlonline.com/IMG/pdf/archives_mm_gm_monarchies-2.pdf]. Manuel Alcaraz in Mercurio-3, "publicly known data of the royal family."
--------
Sy Scholfield quotes 12:36 PM in an article: "Lorsqu’on apprit, à Madrid, que la princesse Sophie avait quitté le palais de la Zarzuela pour la clinique Notre-Dame-de-Lorette, en plein centre de la ville, des groupes de monarchistes, auxquels s’étaient joints des badauds, firent immédiatement route vers cet établissement, afin d’apprendre plus vite la naissance de celui qu’on appelait prématurément "l’héritier du trône d’Espagne". Lorsqu'on dit, à 13 heures, qu'il s'agissait d'une princesse née à 12 h 36, il y eut dans la foule quelques remous de déception avant les traditionnels applaudissements."
("Dans les archives de Point de Vue : la naissance de l'infante Cristina, le 13 juin 1965," ''Point de Vue'', 13 June 2025 [https://www.pointdevue.fr/royal/espagne/dans-les-archives-de-point-de-vue-la-naissance-de-linfante-cristina-le-13-juin-1965]).
Translation: When it was learned in Madrid that Princess Sofia had left the Zarzuela Palace for the Loreto Clinic in the city center, groups of monarchists, joined by onlookers, immediately headed to the facility to quickly learn of the birth of the man prematurely dubbed "the heir to the Spanish throne." When it was announced at 1:00 p.m. that the princess had been born at 12:36 p.m., there were a few ripples of disappointment in the crowd before the traditional applause.
("In the Point de Vue archives: the birth of Infanta Cristina, 13 June 1965").

Sy Scholfield cites an astro-profile giving Aquarius rising, as reported in "All About Modeling," The Milwaukee Sentinel, 18 January 1995, p. 8C: "The Winter 1995 issue of . . . TopModel, published by the company that brings you Elle magazine . . . features superdiva Naomi Campbell on the cover and devotes no less than 24 pages to her . . . The guided tour of all things Naomi includes . . . an astrological profile (she's a Gemini with Aquarius rising)." text_data.shortbiography: Swedish royalty, the daughter of King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden and Maria ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
On 12 August 2014, Sy Scholfield changed the time to 8pm, quoting from the Swedish book, "Ur drottning Kristinas liv och historia: berättelser ur svenska historien" [From Queen Christina's life and history: stories from Swedish history] by Anders Tidner (1915), p. 6: "Emellertid gick vid det kritiska tillfället allt väl för både föräldrarna och det väntade barnet, som föddes den 8 december 1626 klockan 8 på aftonen. Det var en dotter, den blivande drottning Kristina."
Translation: However, at the critical moment, all went well for both the parents and the expected child, who was born on 8 December 1626 at 8 o'clock in the evening. A daughter, the future Queen Kristina. 

Previously this entry had 11:45am rated C (Orig source not known): Revel in AQ fall/54 quotes biographer Neumann, "The Life of Charlotte of Sweden" (Martin Harvey "Nativitas I" notes the quote of "vers minuit," but also quotes Bernard for the time of 8:46 PM LMT, 28 Leo ASC).
Until correction on 6-aug-2012 the date was wrong, because the Julian date 8 December had been entered as Gregorian.
RR was downgraded to C after this email note: I noticed that your source for this data was a biography written by "Neumann" titled Queen Charlotte of Sweden. Queen Charlotte of Sweden was born about 100 years after Queen Christina and it doesn't seem likely that Christina's birth time would be mentioned in Charlotte's biography. Since the quoted source is from 1954, I don't see much hope for finding the book (I checked WorldCat and found no listing) so I think this entry should be lowered from "B" to "C". What do you think?
Scholfield notes that the book is "The Life of Christina of Sweden" by Alfred Neumann (Hutchinson, 1935), published in German as "Konigin Christine" (1936). The text of the books is difficult to access on Google Books and no time of birth has been found in them. Neumann is described on Wikipedia as "a German writer of novels, stories, poems, plays, and films," not as a biographer, so if a time of birth exists in these books then perhaps it is the result of poetic licence.

public_data.sflname: King of Sweden Carl XVI Gustaf

text_data.shortbiography: Swedish royalty, the king upon the death of his grandfather, Gustaf VI, ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
PT changed this record in late April 2009 upon information provided by an Astro.com forum member who referred to an online copy of a FAX from Cecilia Wilmshardt, the royal family information director (https://www.stjarnastrologen.se/horoskopdata/kungahuset/). The contributing forum member writes that "The [accompanying] article says that on 24 Aug 1995, Stjärnrummet phoned Cecilia Wilmhardt asking for the Royal family's birth data. This was granted immediately and the fax arrived a few hours later. But because there had been a few sources saying the time was 10.20am, they called Wilmhardt again for confirmation. She called back a few minutes later saying that both she and her secretary had checked Sibylla's (the King's mother) medical record again, and it indeed said 10.30. . The coordinates given are for Haga Palace in Stockholm. 
Previously, this record carried a DD rating with a time of 9:20 MET with the following source notes: "Marcello Borges quotes Nicholas Campion (his book on royals, "Born to Reign," unfortunately doesn't state original sources). 
Lescaut quotes Ebertin for B.R.of 10:20 AM; not confirmed. Zodiak gives 10:46 AM, Stockholm, in a Dutch magazine.He was born at the royal palace called Haga, which is in the center/north of Stockholm.Fred Opmeer writes, "Concerning the conflicting/unverified birthtime: I do not have any data myself but will put this as a question on a dutch astrological mailing list and will also send a mail to a swedish site with this question. When I have some results, I will tell you"
Sy Scholfield cites official birth announcement quoted in ''Carl XVI Gustaf - Den motvillige monarken'' by Tove Meyer, Deanne Rauscher and Thomas Sjöberg (Bokförlaget Lind & Co, 2010): "Då vi härigenom meddela Eder den för konungahus och folk glädjande underrättelse, att H.K.H. Hertiginnan av Västerbotten den 30 april 1946 kl. 10.20 blivit lyckligen förlöst med en son..." Translation: We hereby announce that H.R.H. the Duchess of Västerbotten on 30 April 1946 at 10:20 a.m. was happily delivered of a son..." The book adds that the ''Expressen'' newspaper announced 10:30 AM as the time of birth.

text_data.shortbiography: American city, the consolidation of which was dedicated at a flag raising to ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Date from legislation: Gary Brand quotes 1897 New York Laws, Chapter 378, pp. 1-555.

Sy Scholfield quotes from local news report: "The New City Ushered In: Big Parade and Brilliant Display at the Birth of Greater New York," New York Times, 1 January 1898, pp. 1-2: "The flag of Greater New York was officially unfurled over the New York City Hall at midnight by a touch of a button by the major of San Francisco, 3,700 miles away, and the second city of the world came into existence ... as the City Hall clock marked 12, steam whistles sounded, the bands played more vehemently ... and the flag of the new city ... went to the top of the pole over the City Hall ... [thereafter] for fifteen minutes, there was a saturation of light and sound, and then the snow began to come fast..."

Data for inauguration from "Van Wyck at the Helm," New York Times, 2 January 1898, p. 1: "Robert A. Van Wyck became the Mayor of New York at noon yesterday. At that hour the government of the new city was turned over to him by the outgoing Mayors of the three cities which had become boroughs of the metropolis - William L. Strong of Manhattan and the Bronx, Frederick W. Wurster of Brooklyn, and Patrick Gleason of Long Island City. No elaborate ceremony marked Mayor Van Wyck's entrance into office at the City Hall: it was a business affair pure and simple..."

text_data.shortbiography: British royalty, who reigned as King Charles I of Scotland and Ireland from ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Paul Wright quotes a letter from the English Ambassador to his Secretary of State, "On Monday last the King rode to the Queen to Dunfermline and returned yesternight. They never loved better. This night at 11 of the clock the Queen was delivered of a son and word therof this night at about three hours brought to the King."
November 19, 1600 OS. The time was undoubtedly LAT, and inasmuch as the hour is a generally rounded off time, the correction of -11 minutes may be considered along with the necessary rectification.Martin Harvey in AQ Winter/1950 gives 10:04 PM rectified from "between 11 and 12 hours of even," historic testimony found in Lloyd's Evening Post as copies from a manuscript, November 19 OS."
(Gadbury gave 10:02:35 PM, with which Partridge disagreed in 1967, as did Adam. PC quotes NN for 10:00 PM. M.A. May 1907 gives 10:03 PM as "culled from Sibly's Celestial Science of Astrology.")
(Sally Davis quotes Charles Carlton, "Charles I: The Personal Monarch," Routledge, 1983, p.1, for "shortly after midday," " quoting contemporary sources, "Fleming, an astrologer of the period.")

Frank Clifford quotes Carolyn Gerard for B.C., British Entertainers 1997 with 7.45 am.
In 2011, an Astro.com Forum member wrote that the birth certificate gave a time of 8:20 AM in the name of John Charleson. "Per the official birth certificate, his father was John Thomson Charleson, and his mother was Jane Turner Charleson. 
He was born at 8:20 AM on August 11, 1949, at the Eastern General Hospital, Leith, Edinburgh, Scotland. 
His parents' address at the time was 130 Restalrig Road South, in Edinburgh, in the district of Leith. The birth certificate was signed by the registrar and Ian's mother on August 22, 1949. Please note that Ian's birth name was John Charleson, with no middle name. He was named after his father, but called Ian, the Gaelic form of John, from birth (as noted on page xiv of his biography, "For Ian Charleson: A Tribute"). A copy of the birth certificate has been promised to be sent to Astrodienst.

text_data.shortbiography: American singer, songwriter, record producer, and actress, a superstar at the ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
An anonymous source quotes an article in Rolling Stone magazine, 23 February 2006, for time of birth and date [http://www.mariahjournal.com/infozone/magazines/2006/rollingstone/index.shtml]: "When Patricia Carey gave birth to a seven-pound baby girl at 7:27 A.M. on March 27th, 1970, the nurse turned to her and said, "That's gonna be one lucky baby." 

However, Frank Clifford pointed out that, as referenced on Wikipedia in February 2021, Carey's birth notice was published in 1969. ("Recent Births Are Announced", ''The Long-Islander'', Huntington, New York, 10 April 1969, section 2, page 3: "Recent births at Huntington Hospital have been announced as follows ... March 27 Mariah, Mr. and Mrs. Alfred Carey, Huntington"). No time given [https://nyshistoricnewspapers.org/lccn/sn83031119/1969-04-10/ed-1/seq-15/#].

Yahoo wrote in article on her age in March 2017, with sources supporting both birth years. [https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/what-is-mariah-careys-real-age-we-investigate-on-her-48th-or-47th-birthday-122330596.html] Carey graduated high school in 1987 and "at the end of the 1987 school year, she’d have just turned 17 if she was born in 1970, and she has never said she skipped a grade. In fact, in her 1999 Homecoming special, during which she returned to her alma mater for a concert, made it clear she wasn’t a great student — and her teachers and superintendent verified that. It seems unlikely she would have graduated a year early", this supports a 1969 birth year. Brett Ratner, her friend and video director, has said that they are “born a day apart”, his birthday being March 28, 1969. Her mother said Mariah was born in 1970 in a 1999 Oprah interview. Carey herself has said, “I don’t have a birthday, I was just dropped here. It was a fairyland experience.” She has described herself as “eternally 12 years old,” and she plans to remain “oblivious to age". Yahoo's "own search to verify her actual birth" with official documents was "frustratingly fruitless".

NNDB.com states "According to People magazine, Carey was born in 1969. In response to fan inquiries about the correct date, a spokesperson of the magazine issued a statement, "We have a copy of Ms. Carey's driver's license, which lists her birthday as March 27, 1969. Furthermore, we spoke with the administrators at the high school she attended who confirmed that Ms. Carey's birthday is March 27, 1969, as did her management when we made our initial interview'".

Starkman rectified to 27 March 1970 07.16.20 EST Asc 11Tau11'.

On the birth certificates of her twins, Monroe and Moroccan, Carey's date of birth is given as "03/27/1970." [http://images4.fanpop.com/image/photos/22200000/Mariah-s-Twins-Birth-Certificates-mariah-careys-lambs-22216353-605-792.jpg].

text_data.shortbiography: Venezuelan politician and popular president of Venezuela, inaugurated on 2 ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Georgiana quotes Vania Norberto of Brazil for a time of 17:10 from Chavez himself to a Venezuelan astrologer. Monica Dimino, who practiced astrology in Venezuela for many years and retains a huge clientele there wrote: "Hugo Chavez, born July 28, 1954, at 3:30 AM in Sabaneta, Venezuela (8N46, 69W56). The date is well known and established. The hour was given to me by a Chavez acquaintance back in the early 90's when he was arrested for a failed coup. At the time, I was told that Chavez had revealed his birth hour to her because he wanted her to consult an astrologer for him. I did not accept that request because I was dealing with family health issues at the time." 

In December 2007 Sy Scholfield quotes a time of 4 AM from Orlando Albornoz's book, "Academic Populism: Higher Education Policies Under State Control" (Caracas: Universidad Central de Venezuela, 2005), p. 719: "In one unforgettable opportunity on state TV, the President's mother had to explain the time and the circumstances surrounding his birth. By the way, he was born at 4 am, in the middle of unusual rains and winds."
Carlos Dum, astrologer in Caracas, Venezuela, writes in an article [http://www.universo.com.ve/web/articulos/chavez_nac.html] that he called Chavez' mother on the phone: "Luego de colgar a mi interlocutora, decidí llamar al número telefónico que me dieron con serial del interior del país donde tuve la suerte de ser atendido a la primera por la propia madre de Chávez, Doña Elena. Después de las debidas presentaciones y el motivo de la llamada, la pregunta: ¿A qué hora nació su hijo el candidato?... La misma, con voz suave y pausada respondió: “Yo de Huguito no recuerdo bien la hora de su nacimiento, pero si le puedo asegurar que nació entre las 03:00 y 05:00 de la madrugada”. (I do not remember the hour of his birth well, but I can assure you that is was between 3 and 5 am)."
Dum himself corrects the time to 3:25, and we leave it in the middle of the two-hour period, leaving an uncertainty of 1 hour. The Cancer ascendant lasts from 3:35 to 5:40.
In September 2022 Scholfield notes that Chavez gives "2 AM" quoted from his birth certificate in the book ''Hugo Chávez. Mi primera vida: Conversaciones con Hugo Chávez'' (Hugo Chavez. My First Life: Conversations with Hugo Chavez) by Ignacio Ramonet (Penguin Random House, 2014): "Mucha agua, mucha lluvia, y nazco el miércoles 28 de julio “a las dos de la madrugada”, dice la partida de nacimiento." (A lot of water, a lot of rain, and I was born on Wednesday, 28 July “at two in the morning”, says the birth certificate.).

text_data.shortbiography: Discovery of the planet Neptune.
text_data.sourcenotes:
ISAR website newsletter March/2003 quotes Joylyn Hill's "The Discovery of the Outer Planets." On Astro.com, Bjorkstrand quotes "The Neptune File" by Tom Standage, Page 120: Shortly before midnight, after checking a few stars in this way, Galle described a faint star in a particular position, and d'Arrest found that there was no corresponding star in the catalog. "That star," he declared, is not on the map!"
Wikipedia gives 'Neptune was discovered just after midnight (of the 24th) after less than an hour of searching and less than 1 degree from the position Le Verrier had predicted', with this reference: Kollerstrom, N. (2001). "A Neptune Discovery Chronology". The British Case for Co-prediction. University College London. Archived from the original. In this paper the time 00:00:14.6 (12.00.15 am) is given. The notation of time is by the astronomicals standards of that time, as 12h00m14.6s on 23 September. The astronomical day began at noon, 12 hours later than the day in civil time reckoning. The reason for this practice, which ended in 1925, was that during an observation night there would be no change of date.
The confirmation that the object was really Neptune was reached in the following night from 24th to 25th September.

text_data.shortbiography: Spanish king, known as "el Hechizado" (the Bewitched), who reigned from 1665 to ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Arthur Blackwell quotes Wemyss FM No.81 from the Ashmole manuscript, 6 November 1661 NS, giving the time as 13:13:49 UT. Americana Encyclopedia has 11 Nov 1661 as OS. (Also called Charles II of Spain).
A.J. Pearce in "Urania" 1880 (page 123) gives 6 Nov 1661 with a birth time of 1:15 PM LMT, Madrid.

Sy Scholfield quotes from ''La torre: revista general de la Universidad de Puerto Rico'', Issues 29-32 (Universidad de Puerto Rico, 1994):
"El 8 de noviembre de 1661, el rey Felipe IV expresó su regocijo, e indudablemente su alivio, al anunciar que doña Mariana, su segunda esposa, le había proporcionado a él, y también al reino, un heredero: "Domingo 6 de éste a la una del día fue nuestro Señor servido de favorecernos con el feliz parto de la Serenísima Reyna , mi muy cara y muy amada muger , y nacimiento del Príncipe Don Carlos Joseph mi hijo." 
Translation: "On 8 November 1661, King Felipe IV expressed his joy, and undoubtedly his relief, by announcing that Doña Mariana, his second wife, had provided him, and also the kingdom, with an heir: "Sunday the 6th of this [month] at one o'clock in the daytime, our Lord was pleased to favour us with the happy birth to the Most Serene Queen, my very dear and beloved wife, of Prince Don Carlos Joseph, my son."
Same time in another biography, "Carlos II nació el domingo 6 de noviembre de 1661 , a la una del día" [Carlos II was born on Sunday, 6 November 1661, at one o'clock during the daytime] (''Los libros de acuerdos municipales de Santander, siglo XVII'', Volume 1, 2003).

Sy Scholfield quotes official announcement from "Governadores civis de Portugal (Lisboa)" by Albino Lapa (Gráfica Santelmo, 1962), p. 112: "A 28 de Setembro de 1863, sobre o nascimento do Principe D. Carlos, no suplemento do «Diário de Lisboa», dizia-se: «Parte Official -Ministério dos Negócios do Reino -Direcção Geral da Administração Política _ 2. Tendo a Divina Providência felecitado estes reinos com o nascimento de um Principe, que sua Magestade a Rainha deu á luz no dia de hoje pela uma hora e meia da tarde."
Translation: About the birth on 28 September 1863 of Prince Don Carlos, the "Diario de Lisboa" supplement, stated: "Official Part-Ministry of General Affairs of the Kingdom -Directorate Policy Administration _ 2 Having Divine Providence of these kingdoms, her Majesty the Queen gave birth to a prince at one-thirty in the afternoon. 
Same data ("1:30 in the day") from "Resenha das familías titulares e grandes de Portugal, Volume 1" by Albano Anthero da Silveira Pinto and Augusto Romano Sanches de Baêna e Farinha (Visconde) (F.A. da Silva, 1991), p. XV: "Sua Alteza o Príncipe Real D. Carlos, nasceu no Real Paço de Nossa Senhora da Ajuda, pela 1 hora e 30 minutos do dia 28 de Setembro de 1863."
Previously this data had 1:35pm rated C (Orig source not known); quoting Old Moore Mar/1908, same in SS No.166.

The birth hour was provided by the father, and I think it may be not very exact. The child was born on January 23, at home, and the birth document was laid down on January 26.I was surprise to see that Ceausescu is born on 23, because he used to celebrate his anniversary on 26. But we have the official paper...Romania adopted the Gregorian calendar in 1919, so we must add 13 days to obtain the real data, and that is February 5."\nThe original ADB entry gave January 26, 1918, 12:00, Bucuresti Romania and was rated X, (date, no time) with the following source notes: LMR quotes Welcome to the Planet Earth for the date. Taeger Lexikon quotes the Weiss Journal for a speculative 8:00 PM.\n

text_data.shortbiography: British writer, England's chief poet of the Gothic revival and the youngest ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Sy Scholfield quotes from the book ''The Life of Thomas Chatterton, Including His Unpublished Poems and Correspondence'' by John Ross Dix (Hamilton, Adams & Company, 1837), page 366:

"The following memorandum is extracted from a manuscript of Chatterton's father's writing in a blank leaf of a family bible . " Thomas , the son of Thomas and Sarah Chatterton , was born November 20th , 1752 , on a Monday night between six and seven o'clock , and was baptised at St. Mary Redcliff Church the 1st day of January following. Full moon 22nd, at 3 in the afternoon."

Dix infers that the imput of this text written by Bristol librarian and author George Catcott is suspicious because Catcott should have known that Chatterton's father died before Thomas's birth. (However Scholfield notes that the entry in the family bible, if it existed, could have been penned by another family member or associate. "November 20th, 1752" New Style was indeed a Monday. And actually the moon was full at 3 PM on 21 November 1752 NS, not 22).

Previously the birth place in this entry was given as London (on 20 November 1752) calling into question the following: Fowler's quotes Sibly for 6:14 AM, "source unknown." Modern Astrology May/1907 gives the same date as Old Style and the time as 6:00 PM LAT. The style change is not confirmed, as the British calendar changed to NS in September 1752. Taeger quotes the Niehenke databank for the same as "from biography," (not confirmed).

text_data.shortbiography: Swedish royalty, the only son of Carl (Karl/Charles) X and Hedwig Leonara of ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Wemyss in Modern Astrology 3/1932, stated as from Gadbury; same in NN No.660 (November 24 OS, 12:00 PM LAT)

Sy Scholfield quotes alternative date and time of birth from a 1655 entry in the diaries of Patrick Gordon: "Tagebuch des Generalen Patrick Gordon, während seiner Kriegsdienste unter den Schweden und Polen vom Jahre 1655 bis 1661, und seines Aufenthaltes in Russland vom Jahre 1661 bis 1699" (Gedruckt in der Universitäts-buchdruckerei, 1849), p. 41: "Der König von Schweden bekam die Nachricht, von der Geburt eines Prinzen, der ihm den 25ten November a. St. in der Nacht zwischen 12 und 1 Uhr geboren wurde, und den Namen Carolus erhielt." [Translation: The king of Sweden got the news of the birth of a prince, born to him on 25 November at St[ockholm?] between 12 and 1 o'clock in the night, named Carolus].
Scholfield notes another source, "Karl XI" by Alf Åberg (Wahlstrom & Widstrand, 1958), p. 5: "Den 24 november 1655 mellan klockan elva och tolv på natten föddes en prins på Stockholms gamla slott." [Translation: On 24 November 1655 between the hours of eleven and twelve at night was born a prince in Stockholm's old castle]. 
Most sources give the 24th so it is possible the news was received in the first hour of the 25th but the birth occurred in the last hour of the 24th, so midnight between the 24th and 25th is suggested as an alternative birth time.

In September 2014 a new, well researched, biography by Mark Whitacker has the birth time of 3 pm: "on July 12, 1937 , Anna gave birth to a baby boy at three o'clock in the afternoon at German-town Hospital."
Previously, Amir Bey quoted him for 0.30 am in American Astrology 9/l993. 
(Biography: Ronald L. Smith "Cosby," 1988, p.1, gives 3:00 AM. The personal quote will take precedence as the biographer did not elucidate.) Philadelphia is given in Who's Who. The biography does not specify the location of the hospital but says, "He lived in Germantown, a poor district in North Philadelphia."
In 12/2000, Amir Bey writes, "I met him at a jazz club in 1979 and asked him for his birth data. I probably identified myself as an astrologer (21 years ago, hence "probably"), and that was his response. I do not think I confused 0:30 with 3:00, as I wrote down what he told me, which would have been "12:30AM", at Philadelphia, instead of 0:30."

Starkman rectified to 03.14.04 EDT Asc 14Gem47'.

Sy Scholfield quotes him for 12:30pm in a letter dated 27/1/1982 in "Piero Chiara" by Ciro Discepolo (Ricerca '90, 2011), p. 9: "Ma quel che mi ha sorpreso di più nel Suo scritto, è la supposizione di una mia nascita "un po' posteriori alle dodici". In effetti, benché io dica solitamente d'essere nato il 23 marzo 1913 alle ore 12, sono nato, per la precisione, verso le 12 e mezza, almeno da quanto ho saputo da mio padre, che in attesa della mia nascita stava fuori dalla camera con l'orologio in mano."
Abridged translation: Although I usually say that I was born on 23 March 1913 at 12:00 [noon], I was born, to be precise, at about 12:30, at least from what I heard from my father who was waiting at my birth outside the room with the clock in his hand.

text_data.shortbiography: British royalty by marriage, she became the Duchess of Cambridge when she ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Natalie Delahaye writes on 4 September 2017: "In April 2011 I was commissioned by a friend of Prince William and Catherine Middleton to produce a compatibility chart as a wedding gift to the couple who were married on 29 April 2011 at Westminster Abbey, London. Because Catherine’s time of birth has never been officially released, and there is no record of the clock-time on her birth certificate, I was very privileged to be given this information in circumstances that involved no intrusion, or any breach of privacy or trust. Despite being under no contract of confidentiality, I made the decision to wait a few years before sharing it with the astrological world... Catherine Elizabeth Middleton was born at 7 p.m. on 9 January 1982 in Berkshire, England." [http://www.astro.com/astrology/aa_article170904_e.htm]

PT quotes BBC for date and place ("Royal Berkshire Hospital in Reading"), no time. Marc Penfield reports a birth time of 11:33 PM but when questioned said he had obtained it from another astrologer. The latter astrologer said he saw it on a British website but could not locate the website when questioned about it. This time is therefore considered unreliable until further evidence is shown. Ana Rakovic gave 8:28 PM on AstrologyinSerbia.com website according to Paddy de Jabrun; no source. Rakovic also gave sister Pippa a time of 4:40 AM; again no source. In late November 2011, Pamela Young posted the following on the Astro.com Forum: "Re Kate Middleton's birth time - in the book, "William and Kate: a Royal Love Story," by Christopher Andersen (New York: Gallery Books, 2011) it is stated on page 73: 
Although they could not know it at the time, the Middletons took their biggest step toward the top rung of the social ladder on January 9, 1982. That afternoon, Caroline gave birth to blue-eyed Catherine Elizabeth Middleton at the Royal Berkshire Hospital in Reading." Paddy de Jabrun quoted 14:15 as rectified birthtime (ascendant end of Gemini).
An inquiry about the birth time by a data collector was answered politely but in the negative by the Duchess' secretary, in August 2013. Whether to protect her privacy or because the information is not available could not be deduced.

text_data.sourcenotes:
Aberdeen Weekly Journal, Aberdeen, Scotland (July 21, 1884, p. 3):
"The Duchess of Albany was safely delivered of a son at Claremont at eleven o'clock on Saturday night. Both Her Royal Highness and the infant Prince are doing well."

Queen Victoria's journal quoted on that day:
“...about 6, got a telegram, asking me to come at once, else I might be sent for in the night. Lo, I quietly got every thing ready & left, reaching Claremont at 1/4 to 9. It was a beautiful evening for the drive very pleasant, but dusty....I went at once to Helena’s rooms, meeting Pauline (?), at the door of Helena’s sitting room. I remained with dear Helena off (?) (?) the whole time, till the Baby was born, a strong boy, who screamed very loudly, on coming into the world...only got to bed after 2.”
http://www.queenvictoriasjournals.org/

On 7 October 2014, Sy Scholfield adjusted the time to 11:25pm, quoting The London Gazette, 21 July 1884, p. 3321: "at twenty-five minutes past eleven o'clock P.M." https://www.thegazette.co.uk/London/issue/25378/page/3321

text_data.shortbiography: Prussian general and military thinker, whose work Vom Kriege (1832; On War) has ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Arno Müller, vol 2, states 1 June. However, as pointed out by atr, it is explained on German Wikipedia that his father faked records to enter his son into the military. The minimum age was 12 years; decisive was the age at 1 June in the year of admission.

Sy Scholfield quotes church record for 1 July in the biography, "Carl von Clausewitz: Lebensbild eines patriotischen Militars und fortschrittlichen Militärtheoretikers" by Gerhard Förster (Militärverlag der Deutschen Demokratischen Republik, 1983), p. 1797: "Danach wurde Carl Philipp Gottlieb, Sohn des Clausewitz, Friedrich Gabriel, am 1. Juli 1780 abends ½ 4 Uhr geboren, getauft am 9. desselben Monats. Da das Kirchenregister ordentlich geführt wurde, ist es durchaus möglich, daß dieses Geburtsdatum stimmt." [Translation: Carl Philipp Gottlieb, son of Frederick Gabriel Clausewitz, was born at 3:30pm on July 1, 1780, baptized on the 9th of the same month. Since the church register was properly conducted, it is quite possible that this birth is correct."]

The literal translation sounds: "... born at 1:00 before noon". This does surely not mean 'an hour before noon' but it means 'at 1:00 a(nte) m(eridiem)'.

There had been other quotes of the BC published before with 11 am and 1 pm birth times. Both are now considered as misunderstandings of the actual wording.

Personal note by Alois Treindl: During some years in the mid 1980ies, I used to have lunch in the Zürich restaurant ''Vier Linden'' a few times a week, meeting friends. Canetti was a regular lunch customer, often dining with a child which we took for his grandson, but which in fact must have been his only child Johanna, born 1972, when Canetti was already 67 years old. Of course we left the nobel prize winner alone, as is customary in Switzerland. I lived at the time on Scheuchzerstrasse, a street which plays some role in Canettis masterpiece of autobiography. Many years later I met Johanna Canetti in the Literaturhaus Zürich, at the book vernissage of Canetti's biographer, and realized only then that the child at Canetti's lunch table had been this woman.

text_data.sourcenotes: Philippe Lepoivre has 4 am, without naming a source. Sy Scholfield quotes the biography by Hussey ''Venerable Ancestor: The Life and Times of Tz'u Hsi'', with "It was the Hour of the Tiger (four o'clock in the morning)". Scholfield posted a chart on his blog using the stated 4 a.m. time and an ascendant of 29 Libra. (Tz'u Hsi is an older spelling of Pinyin Cíxǐ).\nThe date was 10th month 10th day of the Chinese imperial calendar, or 29 November 1835. Chinese calendar conversion is possible on the Astrodienst data entry page, if it is used in Chinese. In fact, the hour of the Tiger covers the two hours 03:00 - 05:00 am, resulting in Rodden Rating C due to limited accuracy. The Ascendant ranges from 17° Libra (03:00 am) to 11° Scorpio (05:00 am). We have chosen 4:05 AM for 0° Scorpio rising with Saturn conjunct the Ascendant.\n

text_data.shortbiography: Dutch novelist and poet. His oeuvre contains a wide variety of genres: lyric ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Sy Scholfield quotes "De man met de orchidee: Het levensverhaal van Louis Couperus" by Albert Vogel (Nijgh & Van Ditmar, 1973), p. 25: "Op het aangiftebiljet van de Burgerlijke Stand staat dat Louis Marie Anne geboren was om twaalf uur 's nachts op de tiende juni. Dit geeft tot onduidelijkheid aanleiding: hij werd geboren in de nacht van negen op tien juni om twaalf uur onder het sterreteken de Tweelingen. Couperus' geboortehuis op de Mauritskade 11 , een typisch patriciërshuis, geeft al aan dat de sociale status van het gezin hoog lag." 
[Translation: the record at the Registry states that Louis Marie Anne was born at twelve o'clock at night on the tenth of June. This gives rise to confusion: he was born between nine and ten June at midnight under the zodiac sign Gemini. Couperus' birthplace was 11 Mauritskade indicating that the family held high social status.]

SVI comments: A print of the official birth record and its description can be found online: [http://www.vernoeming.nl/louis-couperus Louis Couperus: zijn geboorteakte, huwelijksakte en gezinskaart:]. When one reads it literally "op den tienden dezer, des nachts ten twaalf uur" it clearly states that he was born 10 June 1863 at 12 PM. If it would have been 0h00 AM, the archive would use "des morgens".
But as Scholfield and Koppejan note, his more recent biographers H. de Hoogh Castell and Albert Vogel state that he actually was born in the evening of 9 June 1863, shorty before midnight. His biographers also mention that Couperus celebrated his birthday twice, on the 9th and 10th of June. As the reason for the choice of the parents they give, that their tenth child, born on the 9th of June, had died two years before and they did not want to disturb her birthday.

But actually [http://www.genealogieonline.nl/en/kwartierstaten-louis-couperus-crans-huschka/R27470.php genealogieonline.nl] mentions a Maria Catharina Eleonora Couperus, born 10 June 1861, that died early (23 April 1862), according to Henri van Booven even on her birthday (10 June 1861). His [http://www.elseviermaandschrift.nl/EGM/1929/01/19290101/EGM-19290101-0048/story.pdf Het geslacht Couperus] states:
"Op denzelfden maanddatum waarop het jongste kind, Maria (Catharina Eleonora), den 10en Juni (1861) gestorven was, werd Louis, Marie Anne Couperus, twee jaren later (1863) in dat huis geboren. Er bestond eerst eenigen twijfel aangaande het juiste tijdstip van zijn geboorte en wel of deze in den nacht van den 9en op den 10den, voor het middernachtelijk uur, of daarna geschiedde. Na een onderzoek bleek de geboorte op den 10en te hebben plaats gehad. Couperus zelf had dikwijls schertsend gezegd dat het op den 9en moest gebeurd zijn, aangezien het cijfer 9 in zijn leven altijd een groote rol speelde, en er vele belangrijke gebeurtenissen in zijn bestaan op den 9en eener maand plaats vonden. Deze laatste zoon werd aldus gedoopt naar de voornamen der drie, op de Prinsegracht, jong gestorven zusjes: Louise, Johanna en Maria." 

It translates as: "On the same day of the month, as the youngest child, Maria (Catharina Eleonora), the June 10th (1861) had died, was Louis, Marie Anne Couperus, two years later (1863) born in that house. There was first some doubt about the exact time of his birth and whether it was in the night of the 9th on the 10th, before or after the midnight hour. An investigation revealed that the birth would have taken place in the 10th. Couperus himself often jokingly said that it must have happened on the 9th, as the figure 9 in his life always played a great part, and there were many important events in his life happening on the 9and of the month. The last son was baptised according to the names of the three, on the Prinsengracht, young died sisters: Louise, Joanna, and Mary." 

Conclusion: Municipal Archive gives a clear 10 June 1863 at 12:00 PM (Asc Piscus). But his biographers supposed on wrong grounds 10 June 1863 at 00:05 AM (Asc Piscus) or even 9 June 1863 at 11:55 PM (Asc Aquarius), the times Couperus believed in.

text_data.sourcenotes:
In February 2016 Grazia Bordoni forwarded an article by academics Germana Ernst and Giuseppe Bezza confirming that Campanella was born at 6.30 AM and not PM. Their article, "Una Nativita Manoscitta di Campanella" (in Bruniana & Campanelliana, 2007/2, pp. 711-16) includes a manuscript horoscope for Campanella on page 714, stating the date and time as "1568 Sept. 4, 18:30." 
Alois Treindl writes, "I assume that this means an astronomical definition of the day. We are still on the 4 September at birth, because the astronomical day begins at noon (so that no data change happens during the night when observations are made). 4 Sept 18:30 astronomically means 6.30 am of 5 September in civil reckoning. The time is in LAT (local apparent time). The equation of time tells us that this corresponds to 6:25 am LMT. (I verified by computing Sun at noon LMT and LAT for the given date). If I erect a chart for this date and time, I arrive exactly at the results given in the right column 'positioni computate'. For 6:25 am LMT, UT is 5:19."

Previously, this entry had 6pm, with Sy Scholfield quoting from "Halalí: Zehn Portrats spiegeln den Umgang humaner Gesellschaften mit ihren Talenten" by Moritz Pirol (BoD – Books on Demand, 2009), p. 267: "Am Sonntag, dem 5. September 1568, wurde ihnen gegen sechs Uhr nachmittags ein Sohn geboren, der am vorgeschrieben siebenten Lebenstage auf die Vornamen Giovan Domenico getauft wurde." Translation: On Sunday, September 5, 1568, a son was born to them at six o'clock in the afternoon, baptized as prescribed seven days after birth with the names Giovan Domenico.

text_data.sourcenotes:
Steven Stuckey spoke with San Antonio astrologer, Raul Davila on Dec 12, 2015, and states "Raul originally called me the day after the convention on Oct 20, 2013 to give me the data. I wrote him an email on Dec 12th (2015) to re-confirm the story before publishing" (on an astrological internet mailing group). Here is the published text from Steven Stuckey:- 
"I spoke with San Antonio. Tx. astrologer Raul Davila today to get some more definitive details on the Ted Cruz time. Raul attended the Oct 19, 2013 Texas Federation of Republican Women's State Convention, with his wife, who was an invited guest. As this was a women's convention, there were only a handful of men in attendance, including Ted Cruz (who was the keynote speaker) and Cruz's father, Rafael. Raul was seated at the table with Rafael Cruz and asked him if he knew his son's time of birth. The father couldn't remember and suggested that Raul ask Ted for the time. Raul questioned Ted after the keynote speech, and the reply was that he believed he was born in the "early morning hours, sometime around 1:00 AM"."
(Published Canadian BC, without a time)
Brian McNaughton claimed an June 2014, and again in February 2021 that he had seen a birth certificate in a MSNBC show, two days after Cruz renounced his Candadian citizenship, with a time of 7:34 pm. As there is no proof except the claim "I have seen" we did not add this time as an option.

text_data.shortbiography: American actor, the elder son of actor Charlie Chaplin and his first wife, ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Sy Scholfield quotes from “Chaplin's Young Wife Presents Him with Son; Film World Rejoices,” Los Angeles Times, 29 June 1925, p. 1: “born at 6:10 o’clock yesterday morning … according to studio officials that announced its [the baby son’s] arrival.” Same info in The Billboard, 36.27 (July 4, 1925), p. 91: "announced by spokesmen for the actor ... the babe, which arrived at the Chaplin mansion in Beverly Hills at 6:10 o'clock Sunday morning, June 28, would be named Charles Spencer Chaplin, Jr."

Apparently the studio released the news several weeks after the event because the California Birth Index lists Charles Spencer Chaplin born on 5 May 1925 in Los Angeles, mother's maiden name McMurray (which was Lita Grey's birth surname).

Sy Scholfield quotes from "Autobigrafía: o La vida de un hombre que se realiza en la historia" by Nazario Chávez Aliaga (Librería Editorial "Minerva" Miraflores, 1973), p. 26: "Dicho sea en verdad, nací contra mi gusto y contra mis ganas de no querer nacer a las 6 de la tarde, hora de tribulación y hora de blasfemia, hora que da vergüenza nacer... hora murmuradora... hora inmoral. Nací pues, circunstancialmente, en el pueblecito del Huauco, como hubiera podido nacer en Moscú, Pekín, New York, París, Roma o Madrid."

Translation: It can truly be said that I was born against my will and against my desire of not wanting to be born, at 6 pm, with tribulation and in an hour of blasphemy, an ashamed hour ... an immoral hour. I was born, incidentally, in the village of Huauco, as one would have been born in Moscow, Beijing, New York, Paris, Rome or Madrid.

He was born in the village of Huauco (now called Sucre), located in the Province of Celendin Cajamarca, Peru.

text_data.sourcenotes:
Castellanos quotes the astrologer Virginia Lopez for 16 August 1945, 8:30 AM.
-------------------------------
However, Sy Scholfield notes that Casán has given 2:00 AM in an interview: "Moria Casán, La One de la télévision argentine, a fêté son 78e anniversaire lors d’une fête avec ses amis les plus proches. La femme des médias est née le 16 août 1946 à Buenos Aires..... Pour célébrer son anniversaire, La One a pris le temps de remercier ses fans avec un message sincère : “Eh bien, mon amour, je fête le début de mon anniversaire, je crois que je suis née à 2 heures du matin. Je remercie les gens. ici, à tous ceux qui m’envoient un message. Merci de m’aimer et de m’accompagner.”"

Translation: Moria Casán, "La One" of Argentine television, celebrated her 78th birthday with a party with her closest friends. The media woman was born on 16 August 1946 in Buenos Aires..... To celebrate her birthday, La One took the time to thank her fans with a heartfelt message: “Well, my love, I'm celebrating the beginning of my birthday, I think I was born at 2 a.m. I thank people. here, to everyone who sends me a message. Thank you for loving me and accompanying me.”

("Moria Casán, “La One”, fête ses 78 ans," ''Nouvelles Du Monde'', 19 August 2024 [https://www.nouvelles-du-monde.com/moria-casan-la-one-fete-ses-78-ans/]).
-------------------

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7f1VNSyr8yQ].

text_data.shortbiography: (Note, common lexica including the Wikipedia give Caesar's birth date as 13 ...
text_data.sourcenotes: According to Roman sources, the birth date is 13 July 100 BCE (-99) in the old, pre-Julian Roman calendar. This most probably corresponds to the Julian date 29 June 100 BCE (-99). Correct astronomical/astrological calculations require a Julian or Gregorian calendar date. The calendar conversion to the Julian calendar was made by D. Koch using the table given by Chris Bennett [http://www.instonebrewer.com/TyndaleSites/Egypt/ptolemies/chron/chronology.htm here]. A complete list of Roman sources about the birth of Caesar is given in Paulys Real-Encyclopädie der Classischen Altertumswissenschaft vol. 19 (1918), pp. 186-187. Macrobius in his work Saturnalia I 12,34 states that a.d. quartum Idus Quintiles Iulius procreatus, thus that he was born on 12 Quintilis (= July). But Cassius Dio in his Roman History 47.18.6 states that he was actually born on the day of the ludi Apollinares (solemn games to the god Apollo), thus on 13 Quintilis (July), but that his birthday was celebrated on the previous day because "no other god than Apollo should be celebrated on this day". (Καὶ συνέβαινε γὰρ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ τὰ Ἀπολλώνια γίγνεσθαι, ἐψηφίσαντο τῇ προτεραίᾳ τὰ γενέσια ἀγάλλεσθαι, ὡς καὶ λογίου τινὸς Σιβυλλείου ἀπαγορεύοντος μηδενὶ θεῶν τότε πλὴν τῷ Ἀπόλλωνι ἑορτάζεσθαι.) Most scholars therefore agree that Caesar was born on 13 July. As for the year, Suetonius (Caesar 88) and Appianus (bell. civ. II, 149) state that Caesar was killed in his 56th year of life ( periit sexto et quinquagesimo aetatis anno : atque in deorum numerum relatus est and ἐτελεύτησεν ἔτος ἄγων ἑκτὸν ἐπὶ πεντήκοντα). From this, the birth year can be computed as 100 BCE. On the other hand, Plutarchus (Caesar 69) states that Caesar lived for 56 full years (vixit omnino annos sex et quinquaginta), which suggests the birth year 101 BCE. However it is generally assumed that Plutarchus is in error. Theodor Mommsen (Römische Geschichte, vol. 3, 1866(4), pp. 15-17, footnote) believed that Caesar must have been born in 102 BCE because otherwise he would have been too young at the times he took over curule offices. However, this theory, which is in contradiction with all three authors mentioned above, was rejected in detail by Karl Gottlob Zumpt (De dictatoris Caesaris die et anno natali, 1874). In the proleptic Julian calendar the resulting alternative dates would be 16 June 101 BCE (-100) and 27 June 102 BCE (-101). Caesar was murdered on 15 March (Ides of March) 44 BCE. Unfortunately, after his death there was confusion about the cycle of Julian leap years, and for some time leap days were made every third year. The correct date of death in the Julian calendar is probably 14 March (calculation by D. Koch based on Chris Bennett's table). Astrologically, the 101 BCE chart has interesting transits on the Ides of March 44 BCE: Transit Saturn opposit the Sun, transit Pluto conjunct the Moon, transit Uranus conjunct Mars, and transit Jupiter conjunct Uranus. A former version of this page had 13 July 100 BCE (-99) Julian, which is historically wrong. A rectification by G. Pingitzer to 12:41 pm was also mentioned (without source).

Herbert Coleridge, son of Henry Nelson & Sara Coleridge, was born at Hampstead, at a little past 11 in the forenoon." However, apparently October "11th" is a typo because Sarah Coleridge (Sara's mother), who was in attendance at the birth, wrote of the birth on the 8th of October: "On October 8, she described the event to Poole: "Yesterday forenoon, about 11 o'clock Sara was safely brought to bed of a boy..." ("Sara Coleridge, a Victorian Daughter: Her Life and Essays" by Bradford Keyes Mudge, Yale University Press, 1989, p. 54).\n

text_data.sourcenotes:
Originally this entry had a speculative time of 9pm (rated C) with Sy Scholfield quoting from "Altonaer Nachrichten, " 13 March 1896, p. 3: "Stuttgart, 12. März. Die Herzogin Albrecht von Württemberg ist heute Abend von einem Prinzen entbunden worden" (Stuttgart, 12 March. The Duchess Albrecht von Wurttemberg was this evening delivered of a prince).

Herzogin Margarethe Sophie von Württemberg, Gemahlin des Herzogs Albrecht von Württemberg, ist um 6¼ Uhr Abends von einem Prinzen glücklich entbunden worden." (Stuttgart, 12 March. Duchess Margarethe Sophie of Wurttemberg, wife of Duke Albrecht of Wurttemberg, was happily delivered of a prince at six-fifteen o'clock in the evening).

text_data.shortbiography: Dauphin of France as the eldest son and heir of King Charles VIII and Anne of ...
text_data.sourcenotes:
Sy Scholfield quotes from "Vie de la reine Anne de Bretagne, femme des rois de France Charles VIII et Louis XII: suivie de lettres inédites et de documents originaux" by Antoine Le Roux de Lincy (Curmer, Bibliothèque des Fontaines, 1860), pp. 114-115: "Le 10 octobre 1492, onze mois après la cérémonie des épousailles, Anne de Bretagne, étant au château de Plessis, accoucha d'un fils dont la naissance causa une joie très-vive en France & en Bretagne. ... Le roi, heureux & fier de cette naissance, s'empreffa d'écrire aux gens des cours souveraines une lettre ainsi conçue : « Nos amez & féaux, grâces à Dieu & à Notre-Dame, en viron quatre heures du matin, nostre très chère & très amée compagne, la Reyne, est accouchée d'un beau fils..."; and p. 133: "le 6 décembre [1495], le dauphin était mort."

(Translation: On 10 October 1492, eleven months after the wedding ceremony, Anne de Bretagne, being at the castle of Plessis, gave birth to a son whose birth caused a very lively joy in France and Brittany. The king, happy and proud of the birth, was quick to write a letter to the people of the sovereign courts stating: "Our love and thanks to God and Our Lady, about four o'clock in the morning my dearest and most beloved companion, the Queen, was delivered of a beautiful son ... On 6 December [1495], the dauphin died").
Wikipedia gives 11 October, no source. The date of 10 October is given in various chronologies including Père Anselme's "Histoire genealogique et chronologique de la maison royale de France."
Wikipedia gives death date as 16 November 1495, no source.
